title: FiniteVarianceGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained convex minimization on a real, complete, second-countable Hilbert space E. A minimizer xstar exists with ‖x0−xstar‖≤R and f(x0)−f(xstar)≤Δ.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each call at x returns g(x,ξ) using a fresh IID seed. The jointly measurable oracle is unbiased, E[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x), with E‖g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)‖²≤σ². Only gradient samples are supplied; budgets count individual calls, including batch samples.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: The gradient is differentiable and ‖D(∇f)(x)‖≤L0+L1‖∇f(x)‖ everywhere, with L0>0 and L1≥0.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Uniform central second-moment bound σ², σ≥0; no exponential-tail or almost-sure noise bound is required.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: All parameters are public, including x0, L0, L1, R>0, Δ>0, σ≥0, ε>0 and δ∈(0,1). The objective and oracle distribution are hidden.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/FiniteVarianceGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Instance, spec.valid and spec.admissible

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: A measurable output X must satisfy f(X)−f(xstar)≤ε outside a failure event; no particular iterate or averaging rule is required.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: P(f(X)−f(xstar)>ε)≤δ, with probability over both algorithm randomness and IID oracle seeds, under a fixed oracle-call budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Convex stochastic optimization with gradient-dependent curvature and only finite-variance noise, requiring high-probability objective accuracy, is a meaningful variant of the classical globally smooth benchmark.

descriptionHtml:
Finite-Variance Generalized Smooth Convex Minimization

We consider minimizing a convex function f:E→R on a separable real Hilbert space E. The function f is (L0,L1)-smooth, with L0>0 and L1≥0. A given point x0∈E has distance at most R>0 and objective gap at most Δ>0 from a global minimizer x⋆. The oracle returns an unbiased stochastic gradient with variance at most σ2, where σ≥0, using independent, identically distributed samples. For ε>0 and δ∈(0,1), the goal is a measurable output x¯∈E satisfying P(f(x¯)−f(x⋆)>ε)≤δ, where P is the joint law of the samples and independent algorithm randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E, and ∥⋅∥op denotes the induced operator norm. Let Ω be the measurable sample space. The algorithm receives E, Ω, x0, L0, L1, R, Δ, σ, ε, and δ; the objective and sampling distribution are accessed through the oracle.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity and generalized smoothness). The function f is Fréchet differentiable on E, and its gradient ∇f:E→E is Fréchet differentiable. For every x,y∈E and t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y). Generalized smoothness means that ∥∇2f(x)∥op≤L0+L1∥∇f(x)∥,x∈E, where ∇2f(x) is a bounded linear operator from E to E.

Assumption 2 (Initial distance and objective gap). There exists x⋆∈E such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈E,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R,f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ.

Assumption 3 (Finite-variance stochastic gradients). There exist a probability measure ν on Ω and a jointly measurable map g:E×Ω→E. For every x∈E, the map g(x,⋅) is Bochner integrable under ν, the squared error ∥g(x,⋅)−∇f(x)∥2 is integrable, and Eξ∼ν[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),Eξ∼ν[∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2]≤σ2. At call k≥0, a query x∈E receives g(x,ξk). The sample variables (ξk)k≥0 are measurable and mutually independent, each with law ν, and their joint law is independent of the algorithm’s randomness.

Queries may be made at any point of E. After the allotted oracle calls, the algorithm must return a measurable output x¯ satisfying P(f(x¯)−f(x⋆)>ε)≤δ.

Convex f on a separable real Hilbert space has differentiable gradient and ∥∇2f(x)∥≤L0+L1∥∇f(x)∥. A minimizer x⋆ satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R and f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ. IID samples with marginal p and joint law P feed a jointly measurable oracle g, with integrable g(x,⋅) and squared error, ∫g(x,ω)dp=∇f(x) and ∫∥g(x,ω)−∇f(x)∥2dp≤σ2. Known parameters satisfy L0,R,Δ,ε>0, L1,σ≥0, 0<δ<1. Target: measurable final output x^ with P{f(x^)−f(x⋆)>ε}≤δ. Costs count all stochastic-gradient samples, including pilots, corrections, and padding.

import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.FiniteVarianceGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex

open OracleTemplate

abbrev Params := LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.Params

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid q := 0 < q.L0 ∧ 0 ≤ q.L1 ∧ 0 < q.R ∧ 0 < q.Δ ∧
    0 ≤ q.σ ∧ 0 < q.ε ∧ 0 < q.δ ∧ q.δ < 1
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (g : q.E → q.Ω → q.E) (p : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω)
      (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ω)),
    LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ω) => ξ k) (p : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
    O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
          law := P
          answer := fun _ (_, x) seed => g x seed } ∧
    ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ f ∧
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
    Differentiable ℝ (gradient f) ∧
    (∀ x, ‖fderiv ℝ (gradient f) x‖ ≤ q.L0 + q.L1 * ‖gradient f x‖) ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧ ‖q.x0-xstar‖ ≤ q.R ∧ f q.x0-f xstar ≤ q.Δ) ∧
    LongTails.Setups.StochasticSmoothAndConvex.IsStochasticGradient q.E q.Ω (p : Measure _) f g q.σ
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧ ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      (P : Measure _) {ω | q.ε < f (output ω) - f xstar} ≤ ENNReal.ofReal q.δ

end LongTails.Setups.FiniteVarianceGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
